paras: Lerista ingrami, also known commonly as the McIvor River slider, is a species of skink, a lizard in the family Scincidae. The species is endemic to Queensland in Australia.
The specific name, ingrami, is in honor of Australian herpetologist Glen Joseph Ingram.
The preferred natural habitat of L. ingrami is coastal sand dunes.

For its genus, L. ingrami is slender, very pale, and very small. Its average snout-to-vent length (SVL) is 25 mm (0.98 in). It has four digits on each of its four feet. The eyelid is immovable, with a transparent "spectacle".
L. ingrami is terrestrial and fossorial.
